name: Afterimage: batch recorder for Guilty Gear -Strive- Replay Theater replays through OBS
visual_modality: Full-length RGB video files of in-game replays, captured by the user's own OBS. Resolution, fps and codec come from the OBS settings and the README does not fix them.
license_or_terms: Tool is MIT. The footage is Arc System Works game content, so redistributing it is a separate rights question.
actions_or_telemetry: None from the tool itself. You can pair it with StriveFrameViewer (frame meter in replay mode) or the in-game input display, and with replay metadata from ggst-api-rs (floor, players, characters).
term_relevance: Strive replays can show Roman Cancel/RC in all four colours (Red, Blue, Purple, Yellow), Psych Burst and Gold Psych Burst, Faultless Defense, the R.I.S.C. gauge and Gatlings. Danger Time (Xrd) and Force Roman Cancels (XX) are not in Strive. The README does not mention a HUD or input overlay, so a term can only be checked independently if an overlay mod is also running.
evidence: The README describes a Windows 10/11 and Linux desktop app (alpha release). It checks the setup, steps through the saved-replay list and triggers OBS recording for each replay. It supports batch counts and a safe stop. It needs OBS 28+ with the WebSocket server on.
verification: unverified: searcher-reported, no independent page check

name: GGST Replay Database (replaydatabase.com/ggst; source repo joeycf/ggst-replay-database)
visual_modality: An index of RGB match videos (YouTube channels plus the Replay Theater catalogue). Each match record carries a startSeconds offset inside the longer stream. No frames are hosted.
license_or_terms: The repo and its records have no license. Liquipedia-derived content is CC BY-SA 3.0, character art is from the ArcSys Fan Kit (credit required), and the underlying videos fall under YouTube and uploader terms.
actions_or_telemetry: Match-level metadata only: players, characters per side, patch, date, source and timestamp. No inputs or game state.
term_relevance: High-level Strive play is a dense source of Roman Cancels (incl. Yellow RC/YRC, Fast RC), Psych/Gold Psych Burst, Faultless Defense, R.I.S.C. gauge build-up and Gatlings. The labels would have to come from frame annotation, OCR of the HUD, or commentary transcripts.
evidence: The repo describes a searchable, filterable Strive replay catalogue. Records hold a video id, a fighter and player handle per side, and a startSeconds value for 7,966 segment records. Data files are JSON. The live site lists 25,259 replays, filterable by character, matchup, player, patch and source.
verification: unverified: searcher-reported, no independent page check

actions_or_telemetry: Shows on-screen input history (observing online matches and some offline modes), per-frame startup/active/recovery/advantage on the framebar, and a Cancels Panel that can show YRC windows. RISC gauge, Tension Pulse and Burst Gauge options exist. The README does not describe exporting data to files.

The cancels panel and framebar can independently confirm YRC and RC timing and gatling cancels. Danger Time was not mentioned in the README.
evidence: The README lists the hitbox, hurtbox, pushbox and throwbox overlay, the framebar, input history, a framebar setting for replay mode, replay speed-up, GIF mode, transparent screenshots, a hitbox editor, a RISC gauge option and showYrcWindowsInCancelsPanel. The same author's profile (via a GitHub mirror page) also lists ggxrd_replay_mod, which is undocumented.

name: StatePlay-Dataset (Street Fighter III subset)
visual_modality: RGB gameplay video: 10,000 five-second MP4 clips. Frame rate is not stated on the card.
license_or_terms: Tagged cc-by-nc-4.0. The card says this covers only the text annotations, action and state traces, and documentation; Street Fighter III assets remain Capcom IP. Intended for non-commercial academic research. Code is at https://github.com/Jimntu/StatePlay (Apache-2.0).
actions_or_telemetry: Each clip comes with a Parquet file of per-step controller inputs and game state: timer, both players' health and both players' meters. A metadata CSV adds a text 'prompt' describing NPC behaviour and strategy, a category (Control, Defense or Offense) and an outcome distribution label (normal, Macro_success, Macro_fail, Result_win, Result_lose).
term_relevance: Paired controller inputs plus health and meter changes can check terms independently. license_or_terms: Not stated on the competition page or the GitHub README. Graphics are used courtesy of Dimps (The Rumble Fish 2).
actions_or_telemetry: Yes. Replay files (log/replay) store per frame, for each player: isLeft, action ID (0-55, e.g. STAND_D_DF_FC), action remaining frames, HP, energy, x/y, and an encoded key byte (A, B, C, D, L, R, U). An official analysis tool exports these to CSV. The -df flag dumps full FrameData each frame. Gym API (TeamFightingICE/Gym-FightingICE). Audio data is also available.
term_relevance: Motion-named actions allow input-level checks of DP-style (forward, down, down-forward) and QCB-style (down, down-back) specials. Also guard, throw, air attacks, energy-based supers, whiff punishing and spacing (footsies) from x/y plus action IDs. This is a research game, not commercial-franchise visuals, and has no franchise-specific terms (burst, Power Crush, Krushing Blow).
evidence: The competition site describes 56 actions with a 16.67 ms decision window, delayed game state, a visual-AI path through the display byte buffer, replay files with an analysis tool, and GitHub releases. Slides from the replay-analysis tool give the per-frame replay fields.
verification: unverified: searcher-reported, no independent page check

Game coverage beyond FBNeo arcade titles is not confirmed. No modern-game terms (burst, Power Crush, Krushing Blow).
evidence: Search results say select games support ranked/unranked matches with replays made public on Fightcade's website. FightcadeFBNeo is built on FBNeo with a custom GGPO. A changelog notes an input-overlay option for watching both players' inputs in replays. The convert.guru description treats .fr replays as input logs, not video.
verification: unverified: searcher-reported, no independent page check

license_or_terms: MIT. The wT- fork was archived on 2021-07-31. Memory addresses break after Steam patches, and it needs the user's own copy of Tekken 7 on Windows.
actions_or_telemetry: Reads live game state from Tekken 7 memory: last-move frame data (startup, active frames, frame advantage, hit type), frame-by-frame command input history including cancelable frames, and animation IDs (standing 32769, crouching 32770). MatchRecorder.py and BotRecorder.py appear in the file list, but the README does not confirm that they write to file.
term_relevance: Frame advantage and command history allow direct checks of one frame links, whiff punishing (punishing negative or whiffed moves), FC and crouch states via animation IDs, and the B,B,D/B,* sequence behind Korean Backdash / BDC. Sidestep Canceling, Hopkick (u/f+4) and QCB inputs can be read from the input log. Mid and other hit levels come from the move data.
evidence: The README describes the FrameDataOverlay as 'real time move information read from memory' and documents the pointer chain to the player object. Press coverage says it shows frame advantage, hit type, startup and active frames. Another fork exists at https://github.com/PRoosta/TekkenBot.
verification: unverified: searcher-reported, no independent page check

name: Pokémon Showdown public replay archive and JSON replay endpoints
visual_modality: Animated battle playback in the browser, rendered by the Showdown client from the battle log. No pre-rendered frames or video are offered; frames have to be captured by rendering the replay yourself.

actions_or_telemetry: Each replay comes with its full battle log in Showdown's protocol format, seen from the spectator's side: players, team preview (|poke|), |switch|, |move|, |-damage|, |faint|, |turn| and so on, plus the rating. No key is needed.
term_relevance: Strong for battle jargon. SIM-PROTOCOL documents these message types: |drag| (forced switch from Whirlwind or Roar), which covers phazing; |-crit|, |-miss| and |cant| (e.g. paralysis), which cover hax; |-sidestart| and |-sideend| (hazards set and removed), which cover spin (Rapid Spin) and suicide leads; |faint| followed by |switch| and a KO, which covers revenge kill; Wish followed by |-heal|, which covers Wish Passer; Baton Pass with no preceding |-boost|, which covers Dry Passing and Dry Switch; |-boost| followed by several |faint|, which covers sweepers and stallbreakers. Team preview (Gen 5+ formats) covers Hyper Offense/HO. DragMag applies to Gen 4 OU teams. Bag is not applicable.
evidence: The fetched search.json returned live gen9ou replay metadata. The fetched replay JSON contained a full log with |switch|, |move|, |-damage|, |faint|, |teampreview| and other messages; this sample had no |drag|, |-crit| or |-miss|. SIM-PROTOCOL.md (server repo) documents |drag|, |-crit|, |-miss|, |cant|, |-boost|, |-sidestart| and |poke|.

It also has game state: action state ID and its frame counter, position, percent, shield size, ground/air flag, jumps left, L-cancel status, hitstun left, hitlag frames, attack-based and self-induced speeds, hurtbox state, fastfall/powershield/intangibility flags and the last attack that hit (post-frame update, per the Slippi SPEC.md at https://github.com/project-slippi/slippi-wiki/blob/master/SPEC.md).
term_relevance: The game is Melee. It belongs to the series but is NOT one of the four titles named in the request (Ultimate, Brawl, 64, Project M); Project M copies many Melee mechanics. Wavedash: no dedicated field, but it can be inferred from airdodge action state plus trigger and stick input near the ground, then a ground slide. L-cancel status is stored directly, which helps if LL or SL means L-cancel. DI: stick input during hitstun plus the resulting trajectory. KB: attack-based speed and hitstun. Nair, Bair, Dtilt and Zair (Samus, Link, Young Link) appear as action-state IDs. FAF and landing lag come from the action-state frame counter. Not applicable: tatsu, EWGF, DACUS. DSR is a ruleset term that cannot be seen in frames.
evidence: The card says it is raw Slippi .slp files with full game state and controller inputs for every frame at 60 fps. It needs py-slippi, slippi-js, peppi or libmelee to read. Credited to altf4 on the Slippi Discord (Oct 2020). Handwarmers, doubles and games under 30 s were removed. NTSC Melee. Tournament sets of mixed skill.

The hitstun display helps with KB. The hitbox display helps identify Nair, Bair, Dtilt and Zair. Frame advance can measure FAF and landing lag (LL).

The Code Menu has Hitbox, Hitstun, Body Collision state, Ledge Grab Box and Collision Points (SCD) displays. It also says Dolphin saves netplay replays automatically, managed with a 'Replay Manager'.
